answer: At clipping time the shepherd weighs every fleece and seals the bale with wax, and the seal number is entered in the wool book before the bales leave the hill. A relic fleece slipped in from another flock breaks the seal: the mesa of the bale must weigh what the book says, and a strange fleece tips the scales wrong. Forging the clip means shearing 400 sheep, bribing the wool buyer and paying 9,100, while the cipher seal on each bale is broken open at the mill, so a bale whose fleeces were never weighed is sent back up the hill.
